observations: Photo 0 is a promotional render or stock image, not a photograph of a physical item.
The text 'AD5X' is visible on the top left of the printer frame in photo 0.
The brand 'FLASHFORGE' is visible on the front base in photo 0.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI' is overlaid on the image.
A large watermark 'GENERATIVE CAD' is visible across the center.
The image shows a 3D printer with four filament spools and a printed articulated snake.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows AD5X on the frame
photo 0 shows multiple spools but no physical multi-material switching hardware is clearly identified
photo 0 shows an open-frame design typical of semi-enclosed units

risks.risk: The seller may not physically possess the item.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual printer in a real-world environment with a handwritten note showing the current date and the buyer's name.

risks.risk: The printer may have mechanical or electronic defects hidden by the stock photo.
risks.proof: A video of the printer performing a self-test or completing a calibration cube print.

risks.risk: The multi-color capability and extra spools shown in the render may not be included.
risks.proof: A photo of all included accessories and the specific multi-material station if applicable.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual item in your possession with a handwritten note of today's date.
Video of the printer powered on and navigating the menu.
Photos of the actual print bed and nozzle to check for wear.
response.reason: The seller is using a promotional stock render instead of original photos of the actual item. In remote transactions, the absence of real-world photos is a primary indicator of a potential scam.
